article.title: Why AI Systems Need a Fallback When a Tool Is Unavailable
article.why: Practical AI reliability design: graceful degradation, bounded retries, and safe recovery.
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
AI systems increasingly depend on external tools: search services, databases, APIs, calculators, and internal business systems. A model may reason correctly and still fail because one of those tools is temporarily unavailable. Reliable systems therefore need a fallback strategy, not just a primary tool path.

A fallback does not mean pretending that the failed tool worked. It means defining what the system should do when a dependency cannot be used. In some cases, the safest response is to stop and tell the user that fresh data is unavailable. In other cases, the system may use cached information, a secondary service, or a reduced-function workflow.

The right fallback depends on the consequence of stale or incomplete information. A travel assistant may be able to show an older hotel description while clearly labeling it as potentially outdated. A payment agent should not guess whether a transaction succeeded when the payment API times out. The acceptable fallback is determined by risk.

Retries should also be controlled. Temporary network errors often disappear after a short delay, so one or two retries can improve reliability. But unlimited retries can create duplicate requests, higher cost, or long delays. A retry policy should specify the maximum attempts, waiting strategy, and which errors are safe to retry.

Fallback behavior should be visible in logs. Teams need to know how often the primary tool fails, which fallback was used, and whether the final task still succeeded. Otherwise, a system may appear healthy while quietly depending on degraded paths.

Testing is essential because fallback logic is rarely exercised during normal demonstrations. Evaluation should deliberately simulate unavailable APIs, empty search results, slow responses, invalid formats, and partial data. The question is not only whether the system completes the task, but whether it fails safely when completion is impossible.

User communication matters too. If the system switches to a less reliable source, it should say so when that difference affects the answer. A confident response based on stale data can be worse than a short explanation that the live service is unavailable.

Fallback design can also reduce operational pressure. When a noncritical tool fails, a system with a graceful degraded mode can continue serving users instead of turning every dependency incident into a full outage.

The practical principle is to treat tool failure as a normal operating condition rather than an exceptional surprise. For each important dependency, define what can be retried, what alternative is acceptable, when the system must stop, and what the user should be told.

Robust AI is not only about producing a good answer when every component works. It is also about behaving predictably when one component does not.

Fallbacks should also be designed at different levels. A tool-level fallback handles one unavailable API. A workflow-level fallback may simplify the entire process when several dependencies are degraded. For example, an automated approval workflow might switch to ‘draft only’ mode and require a human to complete the final step.

It is useful to define a degradation ladder in advance. Level one might retry the primary service. Level two might use an approved secondary source. Level three might provide partial information with a warning. Level four might stop the task. This prevents teams from inventing emergency behavior during an incident.

Security requirements still apply during fallback. A secondary tool should not receive broader data access simply because the preferred tool is down. In fact, degraded modes deserve extra attention because temporary workarounds can accidentally bypass normal controls.

Organizations should also measure recovery. How long does the system remain in fallback mode? Does it automatically return to the primary tool when health is restored? Can users tell when the system has recovered? A reliable fallback is not only a safe path into degraded operation; it also includes a controlled path back to normal operation.
paragraphs.zh:
AI 系統越來越依賴外部工具，例如搜尋服務、資料庫、API、計算器與內部業務系統。模型本身推理正確，仍可能因工具暫時不可用而失敗。因此可靠系統需要 fallback strategy，而不只是 primary path。

Fallback 不是假裝失敗的工具有成功，而是先定義 dependency 不能使用時該怎麼辦。有些情況最安全的做法是停止並告訴使用者 fresh data 無法取得；有些則可以使用 cache、secondary service 或降級版 workflow。

正確 fallback 取決於 stale 或 incomplete information 的後果。旅遊助手可以顯示較舊的飯店介紹，但要清楚標示可能過期；付款 Agent 遇到 payment API timeout 時，則絕不能猜交易是否成功。

Retry 也必須受控。短暫 network error 經常重試一兩次就會恢復，但 unlimited retry 可能造成 duplicate request、更多成本或長延遲。

Fallback 行為要留下 log。團隊需要知道 primary tool 多常失敗、用了哪個 fallback、最後 task 是否仍成功。

Evaluation 應主動模擬 API unavailable、empty search result、slow response、invalid format 與 partial data。問題不只是『能不能完成』，而是不能完成時是否安全失敗。

和使用者的溝通同樣重要。如果切換到較不可靠來源，而且會影響答案品質，就應說明。

Fallback 也能降低營運壓力。非關鍵工具故障時，有 graceful degraded mode 的系統可以繼續服務，不必讓每個 dependency incident 都變成 full outage。

實務原則是把 tool failure 當成正常運行條件，而不是意外。對每個重要 dependency 都應先定義：什麼可以 retry、什麼 alternative 可接受、何時必須 stop、以及要告訴 user 什麼。

Fallback 還可以分層。Tool-level fallback 處理單一 API；workflow-level fallback 則在多個 dependency degraded 時簡化整個流程。

可事先設計 degradation ladder：第一層 retry primary service，第二層使用 approved secondary source，第三層提供 partial information 加 warning，第四層停止 task。

降級時 security requirement 仍然適用。Secondary tool 不應因為主工具故障就獲得更廣的 data access。

最後要監控 recovery：系統在 fallback mode 待多久、primary tool 恢復後是否自動返回、user 是否知道已恢復。好的 fallback 不只要安全進入降級，也要有受控的回復正常路徑。
paragraphs.ja:
AI systemはsearch、database、API、calculator、internal business systemなどexternal toolへ依存します。model reasoningが正しくてもtoolが一時的に unavailableなら失敗します。そのためprimary pathだけでなくfallback strategyが必要です。

fallbackは失敗したtoolが成功したふりをすることではありません。dependencyを使えないときの動作を事前定義します。fresh dataが必要なら停止して利用不可を伝え、許容できる場合はcache、secondary service、reduced-function workflowを使います。

どのfallbackが許されるかはstale/incomplete informationのriskで決まります。payment API timeout時にtransaction successを推測してはいけません。

retryも制御します。temporary network errorには1〜2回のretryが有効ですが、unlimited retryはduplicate request、cost、delayを増やします。

fallbackはlogへ残し、primary tool failure頻度、使用fallback、final task successを追跡します。

evaluationではAPI unavailable、empty search result、slow response、invalid format、partial dataを意図的にsimulateします。

source reliabilityが下がるならuserへ伝えます。

fallbackはoutageを減らします。noncritical toolが落ちてもgraceful degraded modeならserviceを継続できます。

tool failureをnormal operating conditionとして扱い、retry可能範囲、acceptable alternative、stop条件、user communicationを定義します。

fallbackにはtool-levelとworkflow-levelがあります。複数dependencyがdegradedならworkflow全体をdraft-onlyにするなど簡略化できます。

degradation ladderも有効です。primary retry、approved secondary source、warning付きpartial info、task stopの順に段階を決めます。

degraded modeでもsecurity requirementは同じです。secondary toolへ余分なaccessを与えてはいけません。

recoveryも測定し、fallback modeの時間、primaryへのreturn、userへの復旧表示まで設計します。fallbackは安全に劣化するだけでなく、安全に正常へ戻る仕組みです。

vocabulary.usage: A fallback defines what happens when a tool fails.
The system can enter a degraded mode.
Each important dependency needs a fallback plan.
Stale data may be unacceptable for payments.
Recovery should be controlled and observable.

phrases.example: Graceful degradation can prevent a full outage.
Use bounded retries for temporary failures.
